transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because I keep messing up small things. Like I’ll write the wrong time on a senior-center class sheet, or measure a board and still cut it just a little short because I missed some small print. It’s not huge, but it keeps happening.
Have you noticed any recent change in your memory or thinking?
I don’t think so. Nothing sudden, anyway. I mean, I misplace things or blank on little details sometimes, but I haven’t noticed some big change in how I think.
Did you have this same kind of trouble with attention to details when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. In grade school, teachers would say I was bright, but I’d forget my books or lose homework. I guess I’d also kind of stare out the window unless someone kept nudging me back on task.
Do these attention slips cause problems for you in more than one part of your life, like both at work and at home?

Yeah… it’s not just one place. I’m not working now, but at the center I’ve backed off helping lead a couple of those DIY workshops because I don’t trust myself not to mix something up. And at home, my wife ends up checking plans so I don’t mess up family visits or things at the center.
Do you often feel anxious or worried even when there isn’t a specific problem in front of you?

I’m not sure… I wouldn’t say I’m worried all the time for no reason. I get concerned about things when they come up, but just sitting around anxious with nothing going on? Not really something I’ve noticed.
Do you often act or speak before thinking?
I don’t think so… not often. I mean, I might say something a little quick now and then, but I haven’t really noticed that being a big problem.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task from start to finish?

Yeah… sometimes. Like at the senior center, if people are talking nearby or my phone lights up, I’ll look over and then I lose where I was—on a form, or whatever I’m building. It’s hard to get back into it.
Compared with a few years ago, have these attention mistakes been getting noticeably worse?

A little, yeah. It’s not dramatic, but it’s what brought me in. I keep making small mistakes—like writing the wrong time on a senior-center class sheet, or measuring a board and still cutting it a bit short because I missed the small print. It’s frustrating.
Have you had any head injury, stroke, or other neurological illness?
Not that I know of, no. I haven’t had anything like that diagnosed.
Do you need help with everyday tasks like managing your medications or paying bills?

Not really with pills or bills, no. But… my wife has been double-checking plans for me more, like family visits or things at the center, so I don’t mix something up. And I’ve backed off leading a couple of DIY workshops because of the mistakes.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak?
Not really. I mean, I might pause now and then, but I haven’t noticed a real problem finding words.
Do any of your close relatives have similar problems with attention or distractibility?
I’m not really sure. I can’t say I’ve noticed that in close family, no.
Have you been having trouble remembering recent conversations?
Sometimes, yeah. Like my wife will tell me something simple—where she moved the cards, say—and a minute later I realize I heard her talking, but I didn’t really take in where she said they were.
Have you gotten lost in places that used to feel familiar to you?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t really gotten lost anywhere familiar.
Has your wife told you that your attention or memory has gotten worse lately?
Yeah… she’s mentioned it. I think it’s been more noticeable since we moved into the condo—about a year or so ago. Maybe a year and a month.
Before about a year ago, did these attention and memory problems feel clearly less noticeable than they do now?
Yeah… I’d say before the move it wasn’t as noticeable. It’s really been interfering more since we moved into the condo, about a year and a month ago.
Do these problems feel different from the kind of distractibility you’ve had most of your life?

I mean… it’s not totally new. I’ve kind of always been distractible. Even back in elementary school, teachers would say I was bright, but I’d forget my books, lose homework, stare out the window… that kind of thing, unless someone kept me on track.
Has your wife noticed that your attention or memory is clearly worse now than it used to be?
Yeah… she seems to think it’s more noticeable now. Mostly since we moved into the condo, about a year and a month ago. That’s when it started getting in the way more.
Have you had trouble remembering appointments or events even when you wrote them down or meant to keep track of them?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I try to write things down sometimes, but I can’t say for sure how often I still miss them. It’s… possible, but I don’t have a clear example right now.
Has your wife noticed a clear decline in your memory or attention compared with how you were a few years ago?
I don’t know if I’d call it a clear decline. She’s mentioned it seems more noticeable lately, but compared to a few years ago… I’m not really sure.

final_diagnosis.reason: The history supports a longstanding pattern of inattentive symptoms beginning in childhood and continuing across settings, with functional impact at home and in volunteer/work-like activities. Although the patient and wife noticed somewhat increased problems over the last year, there is no clear evidence of a distinct acquired neurocognitive syndrome, neurological insult, aphasia, disorientation, or loss of independence in basic instrumental tasks. The presentation is therefore more consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive type, than with another specified mental disorder due to brain damage and dysfunction/physical disease.
